newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Polifin sees modest 1997/8 earnings growth.
newsitem.headline: Polifin sees modest 1997/8 earnings growth.

text.p: South African chemicals firm Polifin Ltd said on Thursday trading conditions would be tough in the current financial year but new projects and expected lower feedstock costs would boost earnings.

"The continuous pursuit of improvement, the commissioning of new projects and expected lower feedstock costs should contribute towards a modest improvement in earnings per share in the new financial year," managing director Trevor Munday said.
But he added that forecast modest South African economic growth and expected weaker international polymer and chemical prices in dollar terms would hit the company in the current year.

Munday said the company's main focus was the seven billion rand Project 2003, which envisages the construction of a 500-600,000 tonnes per annum ethylene cracker together with downstream polymer plants.
Presently feedstock options for this cracker are being prepared by Sapref, Sasol and Mossgass and are due to be submitted to Polifin for evaluation during the final quarter of this year.
Munday said they had extended an invitation to Sentrachem to take a 15 percent stake in Project 2003 and Polifin would retain a 55 percent stake.

During the year under review the board had approved Phase Two of the expansion of the Secunda plant which would increase popylene capacity by a further 80,000 tonnes for export. Phase Two will cost 285 million rand.

He said cash generated in the year exceeded one billion rand for the first time and was used to reduce gearing to three percent from 26 percent, fund capital expenditure of 302 million rand, pay tax and dividends and repay shareholder loans of 183 million rand.

The company reported a rise in earnings for the year to June 25, 1997 to 99 cents per share from 83 cents per share in the past year. Attributable income rose to 543 million rand from 454 in the previous year.
